chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah there is a Caller who calls out: 'Whichever servant upon whom Allah has bestowed favor and expanded his sustenance, yet does not make a pilgrimage to Him once every five years to seek His additional rewards, that one is indeed deprived.'

key_terms.مُنَادِياً: A caller or announcer, specifically a divine one in this context
key_terms.نَوَافِلَهُ: Additional rewards or voluntary acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj if one has the financial means but does not go for five years?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted not as a strict obligation (Wajib) for every five years, but as a strong recommendation (Mustahabb) or a benchmark for maintaining spiritual vitality among the financially capable. The 'divine Caller' signifies a public announcement of spiritual loss, emphasizing that neglecting Hajj despite means is a sign of heedlessness (Ghaflah) that warrants divine censure. This underscores the view that Hajj is a recurring act of gratitude and connection, rather than a one-time duty.
